messages:
jamie: quick arch check needed before I merge this PR — gating on the RFC link + rollout plan. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/9145 RFC: https://rfc.redwood.local/r/kv-routing-2026. Main risks: cross-tenant KV cache semantics, fallback correctness, and SLO delta for p95 under burst. Need an explicit arch ack or a list of concrete concerns to address in follow-up patch. Can someone eyes this today? :eyes:

alex: pinged the RFC earlier, looking now. rough idea: is this a change to router that can be feature-flagged? if so we can do a short canary and watch p95.

jamie: yes feature flag + rollout policy included. Canary plan in PR description under "Rollout & Metrics". TL;DR: 5% traffic for 4h -> 25% for 12h -> full if no regressions. Primary metric: p95 latency and error rate, secondary: model cost per request.

meera: thanks — skimmed the RFC. two quick asks: 1) add an explicit invariant about tenant isolation in the RFC and 2) clarify how the KV cache TTL interacts with model-switching. without that it's hard to reason about correctness during fallback.

jamie: good catches. I can add a short section and a small table showing TTL semantics across model variants. will also add a test vector for cross-tenant keys.

ravi: from infra side, we need a brief note about capacity headroom assumption for the fallback model (what GPU type + reserved slots). otherwise autoscaler might overreact. can you include the target instance type and expected per-node concurrency?

jamie: yes — adding expected c5g-small equivalent numbers and target reserved slots in PR. also adding a rollout playbook snippet for ops.

meera: once those three items are in the RFC/PR, I'm happy to give arch ack. please @meera when updated. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder — ensure runbook attached before canary.

jamie: noted. attaching runbook and test plan in the next hour and will ping. thanks all! :party_popper:
